title: No wrong option alone carries the taught words
statement: No wrong option may be the only one carrying the words the teaching just made prominent, because it pulls the learners who listened hardest toward the wrong answer.
detail: A rewrite of a unit film's narration made two words of a definition prominent in the lines around the word being taught, while the film's closing checkpoint still keyed an older definition and one wrong option carried that vocabulary. The film's plan found the item still answerable but steering the child who listened hardest toward that wrong option, and fixed it by putting the word in the key as well, which removes the pull rather than relying on the child to discount it (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/video/u1-script-and-visual-plan.md`, lines 314-325).

evidence.quote: But the narration now makes "poem" and "sung" salient in the two lines around the word epic, so the child who listened hardest is steered toward the only option carrying that vocabulary, which is the wrong direction. The fix below puts "poem" in the key as well, which removes the pull rather than relying on the child to discount it.
